# ShotLab TOUR

> A golf swing analysis web app. It imports Rapsodo MLM2PRO launch-monitor CSV
> exports and reports gapping, dispersion, recurring faults, a yardage book and
> progress trends — with every claim gated by what the device can actually
> support. Free, no account required, works offline.

The distinguishing feature is what it refuses to say. Consumer launch monitors
measure some things well and other things badly, and most software treats every
number on the screen as equally trustworthy. ShotLab does not.

## How it decides what to report

- **Three metric trust tiers.** Ball speed, club speed, smash factor and carry
  are prescribed from freely. Launch angle, attack angle and club path are shown
  but never prescribed from. Spin rate, spin axis, launch direction and every
  modelled output are never used for advice — consumer-radar spin limits of
  agreement are wider than the entire amateur-to-tour spin gap.
- **Sample floors.** No club mean under 10 shots, no club-path or attack-angle
  claim under 15, no dispersion tail under 30.
- **The golfer's own noise floor.** After a few sessions the app measures each
  golfer's shot-to-shot variation and reports a change as real only when it
  clears that. A move smaller than your own spread is reported as exactly that,
  not as improvement.
- **Conditions change meaning, not just context.** Ball type and surface are
  recorded per session. Range balls widen dispersion severalfold and break
  gapping; mats hide fat strikes. Sessions on different conditions are never
  compared as if the difference were skill.
- **The device does not measure face angle.** The app derives it where it must
  and never states one from a single shot.

## What it does not do

No face angle from one shot. No strokes-gained figure from a club-delivery
metric. No inference of body positions, kinematic sequence or ground forces from
ball data. No prescription from spin. No "+N yards per degree" claims. No
rep-count that "grooves" a change.

## Evidence base

Drills and practice structure come from a documented research base: the guidance
hypothesis (Winstein & Schmidt), contextual interference, errorless learning,
external focus of attention, and quiet eye. A 2024 systematic review of 52 RCTs
underpins the short-game work, with the reviewers' own power limitations carried
alongside the findings. Benchmarks are TrackMan-published; on-course norms are
Shot Scope's 90M-shot sample.

## Technical

Static single-page app: vanilla JavaScript, no build step, no framework.
Installable PWA, works offline via a service worker. Data is stored in the
browser (IndexedDB, off by default) and optionally synced to Supabase behind
row-level security for signed-in users. There is no community feature and no
aggregation across users.
